title: James Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on James chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: James Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of James Chapter 4.

questions.question: In James 4, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'Ye lust, and have not' appears in James 4:2, making it the first among the options listed.

questions.question: What is the reason given for wars and fightings among people in James 4?
questions.explanation: The verse states that wars and fightings come from 'your lusts that war in your members' as found in James 4:1.

questions.question: According to James 4:2, why do people not have what they desire?
questions.explanation: James 4:2 states that people have not because 'ye ask not'.

questions.question: What is said about asking in James 4:3?
options: You receive not because you ask amiss
questions.correctAnswer: You receive not because you ask amiss
questions.explanation: James 4:3 explains that 'ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss'.

questions.question: What does James 4:4 say about friendship with the world?
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'the friendship of the world is enmity with God' found in James 4:4.

questions.question: Who does God resist according to James 4:6?
questions.explanation: James 4:6 states that 'God resisteth the proud'.

questions.question: What does God give to the humble according to James 4:6?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that God 'giveth grace unto the humble' as stated in James 4:6.

questions.question: What does James 4:5 reference about the spirit that dwells in us?
questions.explanation: James 4:5 asks if we think the scripture says in vain, 'The spirit that dwelleth in us lusteth to envy'.

questions.question: What term is used in James 4:4 to describe people who are unfaithful to God?
questions.explanation: The text explicitly calls them 'Ye adulterers and adulteresses' in James 4:4.

questions.question: According to James 4:1, what is the source of conflicts among people?
questions.explanation: James 4:1 indicates that wars and fightings come from 'your lusts'.

questions.question: In James 4:2, what do people do in their desire to have?
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'ye kill, and desire to have'.

questions.question: True or False: God gives grace to the humble according to James 4:6.
questions.explanation: James 4:6 states 'but giveth grace unto the humble', confirming that the statement is true.

questions.question: True or False: According to James 4:3, you receive everything you ask for.
questions.explanation: James 4:3 explains you receive not because you ask amiss, implying that not everything is received.

questions.question: True or False: The friendship of the world is a good thing according to James 4:4.
questions.explanation: James 4:4 states that friendship with the world is 'enmity with God', making the statement false.

questions.question: True or False: The spirit that dwells in us is always peaceful according to James 4:5.
questions.explanation: James 4:5 states that 'the spirit that dwelleth in us lusteth to envy', not that it is always peaceful.

medium.title: James Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from James Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to James 4:7, what should believers do to cause the devil to flee from them?
options: Submit yourselves to God and resist the devil
questions.correctAnswer: Submit yourselves to God and resist the devil
questions.explanation: James 4:7 commands believers to submit to God and resist the devil, promising the devil will flee.

questions.question: What does James 4:8 promise will happen if someone submits to God as commanded in James 4:7?
options: God will draw nigh to them
They will be free from all troubles
questions.correctAnswer: God will draw nigh to them
questions.explanation: James 4:8 follows 4:7 and promises that if believers draw nigh to God, God will draw nigh to them.

questions.question: What does James 4:10 say will happen if you humble yourself in the sight of the Lord?
options: You will be free from sin
You will be judged less harshly
questions.explanation: James 4:10 clearly states that those who humble themselves before the Lord will be lifted up by Him.

questions.question: How does James 4:11 explain the relationship between speaking evil of a brother and judging the law as stated in James 4:12?
options: Speaking evil of a brother is judging the law, but there is only one Lawgiver
Judging the law is encouraged to maintain order
Speaking evil is unrelated to judging the law
Judging the law puts one above God
questions.correctAnswer: Speaking evil of a brother is judging the law, but there is only one Lawgiver
questions.explanation: James 4:11 says speaking evil of a brother equates to judging the law, yet James 4:12 reminds us there is only one Lawgiver who can save and destroy.

questions.question: According to James 4:8, what are believers urged to do to draw closer to God?
options: Cleanse your hands and purify your hearts
questions.correctAnswer: Cleanse your hands and purify your hearts
questions.explanation: James 4:8 commands cleansing hands and purifying hearts as actions to draw near to God.

questions.question: What attitude does James 4:6 say God resists, and to whom does He give grace?
options: God resists the proud and gives grace to the humble
God resists the poor and gives grace to the rich
God resists the sinners and gives grace to the righteous
God resists the weak and gives grace to the strong
questions.correctAnswer: God resists the proud and gives grace to the humble
questions.explanation: James 4:6 states that God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble.

questions.question: What does James 4:9 instruct believers to do in response to their sins and worldliness?
questions.explanation: James 4:9 instructs believers to be afflicted, mourn, and weep as a sign of repentance and humility.

questions.question: Why does James 4:3 say some requests are not granted?
options: Because they ask amiss, to consume it on their lusts
Because they do not fast enough
questions.correctAnswer: Because they ask amiss, to consume it on their lusts
questions.explanation: James 4:3 explains that requests are denied because they are made with wrong motives, to satisfy selfish desires.

questions.question: What does James 4:4 say about the friendship of the world?
options: It is necessary for social life
questions.explanation: James 4:4 calls friendship with the world enmity with God, warning against worldly alliances.

questions.question: What does James 4:5 say about the spirit that dwells in us?
questions.explanation: James 4:5 quotes scripture saying the spirit within us lusts to envy, showing inner conflict.

questions.question: According to James 4:12, who is the only one able to save and destroy?
questions.explanation: James 4:12 declares there is only one Lawgiver who can save and destroy, affirming God's unique authority.

questions.question: What is the consequence of judging another according to James 4:12?
options: You take on the role of judge, but there is only one Lawgiver
questions.correctAnswer: You take on the role of judge, but there is only one Lawgiver
questions.explanation: James 4:12 warns that judging another is assuming a role reserved for God alone, the one Lawgiver.

questions.question: True or False: James 4:7 instructs believers to resist the devil after submitting to God.
questions.explanation: James 4:7 clearly commands submission to God followed by resisting the devil.

questions.question: True or False: According to James 4:11, it is acceptable to speak evil of your brother if you judge the law correctly.
questions.explanation: James 4:11 forbids speaking evil of a brother, stating that doing so judges the law, which is improper.

questions.question: True or False: James 4:6 states that God gives grace to the proud and resists the humble.
questions.explanation: James 4:6 says God resists the proud and gives grace to the humble, the opposite of the statement.

hard.title: James Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from James Chapter 4.

questions.question: What do those who plan their future without considering God's will demonstrate according to James 4:13?
questions.explanation: This is supported by James 4:16 which states, 'But now ye rejoice in your boastings: all such rejoicing is evil.'

questions.question: According to James 4:14, what is life compared to?
questions.explanation: James 4:14 says, 'For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.'

questions.question: What should one say when making plans according to James 4:15?
questions.explanation: James 4:15 states, 'For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.'

questions.question: What is the consequence of knowing what is good and not doing it, according to James 4:17?
questions.explanation: James 4:17 declares, 'Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.'

questions.question: In James 4:13, what do the people plan to do?
questions.explanation: James 4:13 states, 'Go to now, ye that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city...'

questions.question: What does James 4:16 imply about pride?
questions.explanation: James 4:16 indicates, 'But now ye rejoice in your boastings: all such rejoicing is evil.'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'katharizo' in James 4:8 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Katharizo' means 'to purify'. This relates to the call to cleanse ourselves in James 4:8.

questions.question: Which literary device is exemplified in James 4:10's statement about humility?
questions.explanation: James 4:10 demonstrates parallelism, contrasting humility before God with being lifted up by Him.

questions.question: Which passage reflects the theme of humility found in James 4:10?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 3:34 states, 'Surely He scorns the scornful, but gives grace to the humble,' aligning with the theme of humility in James 4:10.

questions.question: Which verse in James 4 precedes the discussion on plans for tomorrow?
questions.explanation: James 4:12, discussing the lawgiver, directly precedes the verse on planning in James 4:13.

questions.question: Which verse follows the exhortation regarding asking amiss in James 4:3?
questions.explanation: James 4:4 follows the exhortation in James 4:3, highlighting the enmity with God.

questions.question: The Greek word 'phronesis' used in James 4:16 translates to what concept?
questions.explanation: 'Phronesis' relates to wisdom or practical judgment, which contrasts the boasting mentioned in James 4:16.

questions.question: Which Old Testament figure exemplifies the humility expressed in James 4:10?
questions.explanation: Moses is noted for his humility in Numbers 12:3, reflecting the principle in James 4:10.

questions.question: According to James 4:6, God gives grace to the humble.
questions.explanation: James 4:6 states, 'but giveth grace unto the humble,' affirming the truth of the statement.

questions.question: James 4:3 states that you receive because you ask with the right intentions.
questions.explanation: James 4:3 explains, 'Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss,' indicating the need for right intentions in asking.

theological.title: James Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from James Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does James 4:1 teach about human sin?
options: Human conflicts arise from internal sinful desires
Human sin is primarily outward disobedience
Sin originates from demonic influence only
Wars and fightings are a test from God
questions.correctAnswer: Human conflicts arise from internal sinful desires
questions.explanation: James 4:1 explains that wars and fightings come from lusts that war within the members, indicating sin originates in inward desires.

questions.question: What doctrine does James 4:6 teach about God's grace and human humility?
options: God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble
God gives grace only to the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble
questions.explanation: James 4:6 states that God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble, emphasizing the necessity of humility to receive grace.

questions.question: What doctrine does James 4:12 teach about divine authority and human judgment?
options: Only God is the lawgiver and judge, humans should not judge others
Humans have equal authority to judge others
Judging others is a divine prerogative shared with humans
Law is subject to human interpretation over divine command
questions.correctAnswer: Only God is the lawgiver and judge, humans should not judge others
questions.explanation: James 4:12 declares there is one lawgiver and judge, God, and questions the authority of humans to judge others.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does James 4:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: James 4:7 calls believers to submit to God and resist the devil, demonstrating God's sovereignty over spiritual forces.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does James 4:8 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: James 4:8 exhorts sinners to cleanse their hands and purify their hearts, highlighting God's attribute of holiness requiring purity.

questions.question: How does James 4:10 connect to the broader biblical theme of exaltation and humility?
options: Humble yourselves so God can exalt you
Exaltation comes through wealth and power
Humility is irrelevant to God's plans
God exalts only the righteous by birth
questions.correctAnswer: Humble yourselves so God can exalt you
questions.explanation: James 4:10 teaches humility before God leads to exaltation, connecting with biblical themes like Proverbs 3:34 and 1 Peter 5:6.

questions.question: How does James 4:13–15 prepare for New Testament teaching on human dependence on God's will?
options: Plans must be made acknowledging God’s sovereign will
Human plans are always certain and reliable
God’s will is irrelevant to daily life
Planning is a sign of unbelief
questions.correctAnswer: Plans must be made acknowledging God’s sovereign will
questions.explanation: James 4:13–15 emphasizes saying 'If the Lord will' when making plans, underscoring dependence on God's sovereign will.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses James 4:2 and James 4:3 teach about prayer and human desire?
options: Unfulfilled desires result from asking wrongly to satisfy lust
Human desires are irrelevant to prayer
God grants all desires without condition
questions.correctAnswer: Unfulfilled desires result from asking wrongly to satisfy lust
questions.explanation: James 4:2–3 explains that people do not receive because they ask amiss to consume on their lusts, linking desire and improper prayer.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses James 4:4 and James 4:5 teach about friendship with the world and spiritual envy?
options: Friendship with the world is enmity with God, and the spirit within lusts to envy
Friendship with the world pleases God
Envy is unrelated to spiritual condition
The spirit within us is free from envy
questions.correctAnswer: Friendship with the world is enmity with God, and the spirit within lusts to envy
questions.explanation: James 4:4–5 teaches that being a friend of the world opposes God and that the spirit dwelling in us lusts to envy, highlighting spiritual conflict.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses James 4:11 and James 4:12 teach about judging others and the law?
options: Judging others is improper since only God is the lawgiver and judge
Believers must judge each other strictly
Judging others is an expression of obeying the law
questions.correctAnswer: Judging others is improper since only God is the lawgiver and judge
questions.explanation: James 4:11–12 teaches that speaking evil and judging brothers makes one a judge of the law, but only God is the true lawgiver and judge.

questions.question: Sceptics claim James 4:13–17 promotes a fatalistic attitude that discourages planning. What does James 4:13–17 actually teach?
options: Believers should plan but always with submission to God’s will
God’s will is unknowable so planning is pointless
questions.correctAnswer: Believers should plan but always with submission to God’s will
questions.explanation: James 4:13–17 teaches that while making plans, believers must say 'If the Lord will,' showing responsible planning under God’s sovereignty.

questions.question: What doctrine does James 4:17 teach about moral responsibility and sin?
options: Knowing to do good and not doing it is sin
Sin is only commission, not omission
questions.correctAnswer: Knowing to do good and not doing it is sin
questions.explanation: James 4:17 clearly states that omission of known good is sin, emphasizing moral responsibility beyond actions.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does James 4:6 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: James 4:6 states ‘He giveth more grace,’ demonstrating God’s attribute of grace toward the humble.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do James 4:8 and James 4:9 teach about sanctification and repentance?
options: Drawing near to God requires cleansing and godly sorrow
questions.correctAnswer: Drawing near to God requires cleansing and godly sorrow
questions.explanation: James 4:8–9 links drawing near to God with cleansing hands, purifying hearts, and a turning of laughter to mourning, highlighting repentance in sanctification.

questions.question: How does James 4:1–3 connect to the theme of spiritual warfare in the New Testament?
options: Internal lusts fuel conflict, indicating an ongoing spiritual battle
Spiritual warfare is only against external forces
Lust is unrelated to spiritual struggle
questions.correctAnswer: Internal lusts fuel conflict, indicating an ongoing spiritual battle
questions.explanation: James 4:1–3 describes lusts warring within members as the cause of conflicts, illustrating the spiritual warfare theme present in Ephesians 6.
